title: World history and geography
audience: a high-school student (grades 9–12) or an adult reviewing high-school work
purpose: Explain world history from early civilizations through classical empires, religions, global exchange, revolutions, industrialization, imperialism, the World Wars, decolonization and globalization, including the history of epidemics and medicine.

weeks.12: Epidemics and the history of medicine

blocks.deliverable: Compare the governments of two classical empires.
Map the spread of three religions along trade routes.
Explain the Columbian Exchange's effects on health and populations.
Week 7 midterm; link industrial cities to public-health reform.
Explain causes and consequences of the two World Wars.
Trace how one epidemic changed medicine.
Submit the project; take an unseen 60 minute final in week 14.

project: History of a disease: trace one epidemic, such as cholera or smallpox, through primary and secondary sources and explain how it changed medicine and society.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
